solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chief police officer connected with sex cases

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the sexual word wraps around the officer

parts.note: carnal means relating to bodily, sexual desire
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A senior policeman is linked to a string of sex crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like a noun (court cases) but works as a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means principal or of foremost importance, as in cardinal sins.

clue.text: Conservative replaces leader of union in Hackney?

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes the place of the first letter of the union word

parts.note: a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: A Tory ousts a trade union boss in the London borough of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough; it is the hackney carriage, a horse-drawn or licensed cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is a horse-drawn vehicle for hire, the hackney carriage, an example of the defined class.

clue.text: Restore electron emitted by mysterious charged particle

indicators.note: something emitted is given off, so the letter leaves the combined words

parts.note: recondite means obscure or abstruse
E is the symbol for an electron
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A physics picture: putting things right after an electron is released by a strange ion.
explanation.definitionFit: To recondition is to overhaul or renovate, bringing back into good working order.

clue.text: Cross about Bury firm's clothing

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the firm word wraps around the short letter

parts.note: firm is set, as jelly sets; the 's reads as 'is'
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Angry about a Lancashire company's clothing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town; 'Cross' looks like angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that intersect cross each other.

clue.text: Con cleaning out good person once more

indicators.note: cleaning something out removes it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
ST, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A trickster empties out a decent person's pockets yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle or convict, but it means against.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, repeated.

clue.text: Less sensitive issue

definitions.meaning: more numb, the comparative of numb, spelt the same as the word for a figure

explanation.surface: A matter on which people feel less strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb gives the comparative, and a magazine's edition is called a number or issue.

clue.text: Make one and one equal to begin with

parts.note: a unit is one

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Combine two singles so they are equal from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together into a single whole.

clue.text: Farewell aside to the audience

indicators.note: what is spoken to an audience is heard, so the word's sound counts

parts.note: by means aside, as in put by or by the way

explanation.surface: An actor's goodbye muttered as a stage aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye is a short form of goodbye, a parting word.

clue.text: Prepare to discover the meaning of unknown quantity

parts.note: to read a situation or riddle is to make sense of it
y is a standard unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Get set to work out what an unknown means.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready something is to make it prepared, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Broadcaster's dropped Christmas programme

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: shed is dropped and Yule is Christmas

explanation.surface: A TV channel has axed its festive show.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the answer is said 'shed-yule'.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or plan of events, a programme.

clue.text: Apricot tart contains dairy

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer within their letters, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A fruit pastry with a creamy filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is an Italian soft cheese, a dairy product.

clue.text: Primate with time for priest's wild vision

indicators.note: one thing put in for another is substituted for it, so time takes the priest's place

parts.note: a chimp is a primate
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An ape with time to spare for a clergyman's fantastic dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like a church title beside 'priest', but it is the ape CHIMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful illusion or impossible dream, originally a mythical monster.

clue.text: Can region spread enlightenment? Absolutely not!

indicators.note: letters spread about are scattered and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Could a district promote enlightened thinking? Certainly not!
explanation.definitionFit: The exact opposite of enlightenment is lack of knowledge, so the definition works by negation.

clue.text: Minute appearance of actor on stage

definitions.meaning: a minute is a written record, an item entered in a log
an actor's entrance onto the stage

explanation.surface: A brief moment when an actor walks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like tiny or sixty seconds; here it is a noted record.
explanation.definitionFit: An item recorded in minutes is a written record; a performer's arrival on stage is also called this.

clue.text: Rioter burst into hearing related to land

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

indicators.note: something burst is broken apart, so its letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A rioter bursts into a court hearing about a land dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' scrambles the rioter's letters, and 'into' places that scramble inside the hearing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Territorial concerns territory, an area of land.

clue.text: Harsh electronic form of music

parts.note: grim means stern or harsh

explanation.surface: A grating style of electronic music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electronic' seems to describe the music, but it only supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is a British urban music genre that emerged in London in the early 2000s.

clue.text: Layabout hit sentry out of uniform

parts.note: to slug is to hit hard

indicators.note: something out of a thing is missing from it, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a guard is a sentry
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An idler strikes a soldier who is out of his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of uniform' reads as off-duty dress; it means GUARD loses its U.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggard is a lazy, idle person, the same as a layabout.

clue.text: Bridge partnership stops priest playing Old Maid

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so the partnership sits inside the other letters
playing about with letters rearranges them

parts.note: North and South form one partnership at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Card players halt a cleric playing the card game Old Maid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges PRIEST to SPITER, and 'stops' plugs NS in.
explanation.definitionFit: Old maid is a dated, unkind term for an unmarried older woman.

clue.text: Send up husband and father beginning to believe extravagant nonsense

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up lifts the letters to read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: big means grand or lavish

explanation.surface: Mock a husband and father for starting to believe extravagant rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' looks like mock, but reverses H + SIRE + B + BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberish is unintelligible or meaningless talk.

clue.text: Believe head of state's a tool of the Treasury?

parts.note: to reckon is to believe or suppose
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen, the British head of state

explanation.surface: Think the monarch is a mere puppet of the finance ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: A ready reckoner is a book of tables for quick calculations, fitting a ministry of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckoner is a calculating aid, apt for the Treasury, the UK finance ministry.

clue.text: Family group has assistance withdrawn before vitriolic attack

indicators.note: the reversed word comes ahead of the family group
something drawn back is pulled backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: aid is assistance
a tribe is a family or kinship group

explanation.surface: A clan has its support taken away just before a savage tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack or tirade.

clue.text: Sit on horse led by British groom's mate

indicators.note: the British letter goes in front of the riding word

parts.note: to ride is to sit on a horse and travel

explanation.surface: A British rider with a stable groom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' suggests a stable hand with horses; here it is the bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom's partner at a wedding is the woman he marries.

clue.text: Ancient philosopher connecting prophecy with Nicodemus

indicators.note: connecting ... with is a split hidden-word signal: only the tail of the first word joins up with the next
with pairs the second word to the first, and only its opening letters complete the joined run

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker linking a prediction to the biblical Nicodemus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'connecting ... with' splits round 'prophecy': its last two letters join the first three of 'Nicodemus', skipping the word 'with' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cynics were a school of Greek thinkers, such as Diogenes, who scorned convention.

clue.text: Notice club's top rugby player

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: Spot the leading player at a rugby club.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock something is informal British for to notice it.

clue.text: Press put down object of affection

definitions.meaning: to ... a revolt is to put it down

explanation.surface: Newspapers belittle someone's sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezing hard, suppressing a revolt, and an infatuation are all senses of the word.

clue.text: JFK or Nixon could be seen as a product of the Masons?

definitions.text: JFK or Nixon could be seen as
definitions.meaning: JFK and Nixon are films directed by Oliver Stone
masonry, carved or laid stone, is made by masons

explanation.surface: Presidents portrayed as creations of the Freemasons, a conspiracy theory.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital in Masons hints at Freemasons, but it means stonemasons; JFK and Nixon are Oliver Stone films.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry built of cut stone is what stonemasons produce; a film by director Oliver Stone is his work.

clue.text: Upset about parking in middle of road works

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the others
the inner letters of the word, its ends removed

parts.note: P is the parking sign

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Angry about parking in the middle of the road during roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' is the plural of opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a plural of opus, so it means works, as well as the musical drama.

clue.text: Little-known remedy for patient being deprived of lead?

indicators.note: the remedy is for the patient, so the patient's name comes first as the possessive
losing its lead means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Job of the Bible is the byword for patience, so the patient's is Job's
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: An obscure treatment for someone ill who has lost their leading position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a sick person, but it is Job, famed for patience: JOB'S CURE without J.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is little known or not widely recognised.

clue.text: Go downhill rapidly and almost miss out

indicators.note: almost the whole word means its last letter is cut off

parts.note: to skip is to miss out

explanation.surface: Slide quickly down a slope and nearly avoid it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go downhill' looks like decline; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to glide downhill on skis.

clue.text: Number one trend turned into issue

indicators.note: turned round means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tide is a trend, as in the tide of opinion

explanation.surface: A leading fashion that has become a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like top spot; it is NO + I, then TIDE, all reversed by 'turned'.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a publication is one of its editions.

clue.text: Think about inspiring good man

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the shuffled letters take in another
letters moved about are rearranged

explanation.surface: Consider inspiring a virtuous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges THINK, which then takes in G.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess each piece is called a man, and one such piece moves in an L-shape.

clue.text: Single male part transposed by composer

parts.note: J.S. Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: transposed here means turned round end to end, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: A musical part rearranged by a great composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposed' suggests a key change in music; here ROLE is reversed to ELOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man.
